newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan farmers protest over imports.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan farmers protest over imports.

text.p: Farmers and agricultural workers in more than half of Venezuela's 22 states held marches and blocked roads Tuesday to protest government farming policies and the flood of food imports.
The day of protest was against, "the government's mistaken policy for the agricultural sector which favors imports," said Hiram Gaviria, president of the farm workers organization Fedeagro.

Farmers complain that low import duties and lack of subsidies for the agricultural sector favor cheap imports and concentrate wealth in a handful of agro-industrial companies which buy both local and imported produce.
The elimination last week of preferential lending rates for the agricultural sector will boost the inflow of imports, farming groups have said.
Gaviria, a former agricultural minister, said another large protest would be carried out on Thursday at the country's second largest port, Puerto Cabello.
Despite a small population of about 23 million people and large areas of prime agricultural land, Venezuela imports much of its food needs, including nearly half of the milk consumed in the country.
